summary: Siew-Yue Killingley was a linguist who earned an M.A. at the University of Malaya (~1962–1966) and a Ph.D. at SOAS (~1969–1972). She taught at St Mary's College, Fenham (1972–1980) and taught linguistics and Chinese at the University of Newcastle.

Sigmund Feist was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied under Heinrich Hübschmann and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Strasbourg (~1885–1888). He served as Director of the Reichenheim Orphanage from 1906 to 1935.

Signe Cohen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Ludo Rocher. She held an attested post at the University of Pennsylvania in 1999 and became a professor at the University of Missouri.

Signe Howell worked in religious studies and other fields, studying at SOAS (~1968–1972) and the University of Oxford (~1974–1980). She taught Heidi Fjeld and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1989.

Sigrid Westphal-Hellbusch earned her Ph.D. at Humboldt University (1935–1940), later serving there as PD (1946) and professor (1951–1953). She held professorships at the Free University of Berlin (1956–1970) and directed the Ethnological Museum of Berlin's West Asian Department (1970–1976).

Sigurd Lindquist was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Karl Ferdinand Johansson (~1914–1920) and earned his Ph.D. at Uppsala University (1914–1932). In 1934, he became a docent at Uppsala University.

Silvia D'Intino is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. Her affiliations include attested posts at Anthropologie et Histoire des Mondes Antiques in 2023 and the Centre national de la recherche scientifique in 2025.

Silvia Luraghi works in linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Turin (1978–1982) and earned a PhD at the University of Pavia (1983–1987), later holding posts at Turin (~1993–1998), Roma Tre (~1998–1999), and Pavia (~1999).

Silvio Trovanelli was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who completed his law studies at the University of Bologna by 1883. He subsequently served as docent of juridical philosophy at the University of Bologna.

Silvio Vita studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton University. In Buddhist studies, sinology, and japanology, his career included professorships at Naples "L'Orientale", Naples Federico II, Rome, and Kyoto, and directing the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

Simo Parpola earned his PhD at the University of Helsinki, also studying at the Pontifical Biblical Institute and British Museum. A scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology, he held posts at Heidelberg, Chicago, and Helsinki, where he became professor in 1978.

Simon Brodbeck is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He served as a research associate at SOAS University of London (attested 2007–2008) and held a post at Cardiff University (attested 2009–2012).

Indologist Simon Cubelic earned degrees from Heidelberg (PhD 2010–2017) and Humboldt University (2019–2023). He held posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Heidelberg University, University of Munich as Professor of Modern Indology, and Göttingen Academy of Sciences.

Simon Matthews Edwin Kempson studied at Cheltenham and Gonville and Caius Colleges. Working in Indology and linguistics, he was headmaster at Bareilly College (1858), taught at Cambridge (1879–1881), and was Professor of Hindustani at Staff College, Camberley (1882–1883).

Simon P. James is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who taught Colette Sciberras. He served at Durham University as a tutor in philosophy (attested 2001) and as a lecturer in philosophy (attested 2013–2014).
Simon Winant is an Indology and linguistics scholar. As attested in 2026, he is a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.

Simon Wong is a Buddhist studies scholar who held an attested post as professor at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology in 2010. He also held a post in Dermatology and Skin Science at the University of British Columbia.
Singhathon Narāsabho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Visva-Bharati University under doctoral supervisor Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti.

Siniruddha Dash works in Indology and linguistics. He served as Director at the University of Madras (2000–2014), the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (attested 2013), and the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation (2020).

Siran Upendra Deraniyagala was an archaeologist who studied under Frank Raymond Allchin at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1960–1966), London (~1966–1968), and Harvard (~1986–1988). He served as Director General of Sri Lanka's Department of Archaeology (~1992–2001).
